root_protocol_proposal.analysis: counts: compare per-level operation counts across arms (deterministic). timers: compare exclusive_ms pieces (sum exactly to the fereg hierarchy phase) descriptively; never add inclusive timers; counter-build times are not evidence.

can_distinguish: whether the candidate serial raw-edge sort does more/fewer comparisons, swaps, partition/insertion steps or heapsort fallbacks than the accepted heapsort at each contraction level, and its meter queries

how the fereg hierarchy phase splits into contraction sort / duplicate reduction / mapping, forest, aggregation, pruning, level finalization, bookkeeping, finest components, coarse centering, terminal factor and remainders
cannot_distinguish: per-operation cost (memory traffic, branches, caches) or any causal kernel claim
work inside team lanes (team/hosted sorts are recorded by size and timed only)
timer overhead is small but nonzero; timer builds are diagnostic, not production timing
limits: no cloud timing, profile, SCC job, plugin build or replay; run() exercised only with mocked native calls
raw logs and prepared copies are session-local and not retained; commands, exits and hashes are recorded here
the standard run_tests.sh still fails at the known installed-plugin binding check; not rerun (no runtime change)

findings: Post-sort duration includes graph allocation, reduction, compaction, invariants and publication, not duplicate summation alone.
Swap calls do not establish exact record moves.
Deleting required per-level timers passed; coverage now follows independently parsed route levels/terminal and the scoped always-prune policy.
One-microsecond nesting slack accepted negative exclusive durations; strict per-level and aggregate nesting now rejects them.
Nonfinite/negative profile durations now reject in either mode.
Per-case determinism now checks each call and stops immediately, retaining the failing outputs.
Source archives now preserve executable status so the documented build entrypoints survive extraction.
